newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-DE AVILA SCORES TWO AS METROSTARS BEAT RAPIDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DE AVILA SCORES TWO AS METROSTARS BEAT RAPIDS.

text.p: Colombian international forward Antony De Avila scored two goals and helped create two others to power the New York/New Jersey MetroStars to a 4-1 victory over the Colorado Rapids in a Major League Soccer game on Sunday.

U.S. international midfielder Tab Ramos, in only his second game back from a serious knee injury, also scored a pair of goals, in the second half, as the MetroStars (6-11) snapped a five-game losing streak. Sean Henderson scored for the Rapids (7-10).
De Avila, who returned to action for the first time with a soft cast on a left arm he broke two weeks ago, entered the game with only two goals and three assists in 11 matches.
The MetroStars are coached by Carlos Alberto Parreira, who directed Brazil to the 1994 World Cup title.

In Columbus, Ohio, the Dallas Burn (10-9), who dropped a 5-0 decision to Chivas (Mexico) in a friendly on Friday, overcame a 1-0 deficit and registered a 1-0 win over the struggling Columbus Crew (7-10), who have lost eight of their last nine matches.

After U.S. national team forward Brian McBride gave the hosts an early 1-0 lead, Wade Webber and Jorge Flores scored for the Burn. The Crew outshot the Burn 31-10 for the game and 21-3 in the second half.
At Tampa Bay, the Mutiny (10-9) retained second place in the Eastern Conference with a 3-2 shootout victory over the San Jose Clash (7-12). The Mutiny prevailed in the tie-breaker 5-3.
Eddie Lewis and El Salvadoran Ronald Cerritos scored for the Clash, Italian Giuseppe Galderisi for the Mutiny.
In Saturday's action, both conference leaders lost.

In Pasadena, the Los Angeles Galaxy (6-11) struck twice in the opening 27 minutes en route to a 3-1 triumph over defending champion and Eastern Conference leaders D.C. United (13-5), who have the best record in the league.
Chris Armas and Ecuadoran Eduardo Hurtado tallied in the opening half and Brazilian Welton added a goal with 11 minutes remaining.

Richie Williams scored for United, who had a pair of foreign players ejected -- Nigerian defender Ben Iroha (for fouling a player on a goal-scoring attempt in the 64th minute) and Bolivian international midfielder Marco Etcheverry (for dissent a minute later).

In Foxboro, Massachusetts, John Kerr and newly acquired Evans Wise of Trinidad & Tobago scored to lift the New England Revolution (11-7) to a 2-0 win over the Kansas City Wizards (12-7), who lead the Western Conference. Former Scottish international Mo Johnston of Kansas City and Alejandro Farias of New England were red-carded with two minutes left.
